_comment: Deny by default, everywhere. The previous version granted .read and .write
on /projects/$projectId to 'auth != null' — any principal that could sign
in to Firebase project shotbreak-9f342 at all could read and overwrite
every production stored there. The Firebase web API key is public by
design (it appears in app.html and js/config.js), so the only thing
standing between an outsider and that data was which sign-in providers
happen to be enabled on the project.
Nothing reads or writes this path. The Studio keeps productions in
localStorage and in Netlify Blobs via projects-sync; app.html uses
firebase.auth() only and never opens firebase.database(). So the grant
bought nothing and is removed rather than narrowed.
Server code that legitimately needs this data uses the Admin SDK, which
bypasses these rules by design. Client access stays closed.
server_secrets holds provider API keys. It was already unreachable by way
of Firebase's implicit deny; it is written out here so that adding a
permissive rule higher up cannot silently open it.
